facts.fact: Internet Society's report lists no submarine cable for Burundi, terrestrial cross-border links to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Rwanda and Tanzania, and says Burundi relies mainly on SEACOM and EASSy for cloud access in South Africa.

ETH.note: Ethiopia is named only as a neighbour of Kenya's land links.

facts.fact: Internet Society's report lists eight submarine cables for Kenya (2Africa, Africa-1, DARE-1, EASSy, LION2, PEACE, SEACOM, TEAMS) and says the regulator reported on 13 May 2024 that TEAMS was used for redundancy.
Internet Society's report lists three submarine cables for Mozambique (2Africa, EASSy, SEACOM) and says SEACOM and EASSy were cut on 12 May 2024 and repaired by 3 June 2024.

Internet Society's report lists no submarine cable for Malawi and terrestrial cross-border links to Mozambique, Tanzania and Zambia, and says Malawi relies mainly on SEACOM and EASSy for cloud access in South Africa.

Internet Society's report lists no submarine cable for Rwanda and terrestrial cross-border links to Burundi, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania and Uganda, and says Rwanda relies mainly on SEACOM and EASSy for cloud access in South Africa.

facts.fact: Internet Society's report lists three submarine cables for Tanzania (EASSy, SEACOM, SEAS) and says Tanzania saw the greatest reduction in internet performance when SEACOM and EASSy were cut on 12 May 2024.
Internet Society's report lists no submarine cable for Uganda, terrestrial cross-border links to five neighbours, and says a Kampala to Mombasa fibre cable delivers submarine capacity to Uganda.
Internet Society's report lists nine submarine cables for South Africa (ACE, EASSy, Equiano, METISS, SEACOM, SAFE, SAT-3, T3, WACS) and terrestrial links to five neighbours.
